VP3 Phone Web Push transport dependency bundle
============================================

The deployment ZIP includes these production dependencies. The server does not
need Composer, a dependency download, an installation script or a Composer plugin.
Keep this directory and its vendor/ subdirectory in the production package.

Worker requirements
-------------------
Run the Phone push worker with PHP 8.2 or newer (the release CI uses PHP 8.3).
The web UI/API and queue may continue running on PHP 8.1. The transport wrapper
checks PHP_VERSION_ID before loading this autoloader and reports
runtime_requires_php82 without making a send attempt on PHP 8.1.

Required PHP extensions: curl, json, mbstring and openssl. OpenSSL must support
prime256v1 (P-256), aes-128-gcm and HMAC SHA-256; cURL must support HTTPS. DNS
resolution and the relevant cURL/OpenSSL functions must be enabled. GMP or BCMath
is an optional performance improvement, not a deployment requirement.

The helper vp3_phone_push_transport_ready_v1() reports local transport capability.
It does not confirm that keys, subscriptions, consent or a real phone are ready.
The worker must check readiness before claiming work. Configuration credentials
remain in the existing protected registry; no secret belongs in this directory.

Pinned upstream software
------------------------
minishlink/web-push v11.0.0 is the maintained PHP 8.2+ release. It supplies the
standards implementations for RFC 8291 aes128gcm and RFC 8292 VAPID/ES256.
nyholm/psr7 1.8.2 supplies explicit PSR-7/PSR-17 message factories. The application
supplies its own PSR-18 transport; the library never chooses an HTTP client for
this send path. All transitive production packages are pinned by composer.lock.
MANIFEST.json records exact versions, original Git commits/dist references,
license paths and SHA-256 hashes for production files. No development packages
are installed. THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt retains all MIT notices in one file, and
the original notices remain with each package and the Composer autoloader.

Upstream release and source:
https://github.com/web-push-libs/web-push-php/releases/tag/v11.0.0
https://github.com/web-push-libs/web-push-php/tree/v11.0.0
https://packagist.org/packages/minishlink/web-push
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8291
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8292

Composer's advisory and abandonment audit reported no findings on 2026-11-24.
The checked timestamp is recorded in MANIFEST.json. Recheck advisories when this
bundle is updated; this historical result is not a promise about future findings.

Reproduce the installed dependencies
-----------------------------------
Use Composer 2.11.3, obtained from https://getcomposer.org/download/2.11.3/composer.phar
and verify its SHA-256 against the official release checksum:
04f8b003da4e3a2459056591fbfebd02b4dc3e5adeb158616b90cf55a65113ec

Run from this directory using a supported PHP executable:

    php composer.phar install --no-dev --no-scripts --no-plugins --prefer-dist --classmap-authoritative --no-interaction
    php composer.phar check-platform-reqs --no-dev
    php composer.phar audit --no-dev --format=json

The Composer binary is not bundled in the application. Use the path where you
downloaded it when running these commands. Never use --ignore-platform-reqs.
config.platform.php=8.2.0 fixes the minimum resolution target; the generated
platform_check.php still enforces the actual PHP version and required extensions.
Exact version constraints are intentional; Composer validate's corresponding
semver recommendations are not errors in the lock or deployment.

Runtime and review boundaries
-----------------------------
The public transport API accepts only the subscription, VAPID key pair/subject
with a verified cached authorization, generic JSON payload and ttl/topic/urgency.
There are no URL, arbitrary header, proxy, CA or
HTTP-client options. Internal callable seams exist only for credential-free
tests. The queue is responsible for current audience and authorization checks.

Apple requires that a VAPID JWT not be refreshed more frequently than once per
hour. vp3_phone_push_transport_vapid_header_v1 is a local signing factory for the
queue's durable encrypted cache; it returns authorization, issued_epoch and
expires_epoch with a 12-hour JWT. Call it only on a permitted cache refresh, not
for every send. The transport requires that cached authorization and verifies
its ES256 signature, provider origin, configured subject and expiration using
the bundled JOSE library before injecting it into WebPush. It never falls back
to per-send JWT generation. Each payload still gets fresh ephemeral encryption
keys and a fresh salt, independently of the reused authentication token.
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/sending-web-push-notifications-in-web-apps-and-browsers

Every attempt revalidates the recognized provider URL and every A/AAAA answer,
rejects private/reserved/tunnel addresses, and pins one public address while
retaining the provider hostname for TLS. No redirects, inherited proxy/netrc
credentials, hidden HTTP retry, response-body storage or exception text logging
is allowed. cURL has at most 3 seconds to connect and 8 seconds total, reduced by
DNS time already spent. Response headers/body stop at 16 KiB/8 KiB. PHP's native
DNS call uses the host resolver's timeout outside cURL's hard deadline; configure
a process-level worker watchdog to bound a stuck resolver. Where the host offers
the timeout command, wrap the worker cron command with timeout 55s. A late DNS
answer is rejected before sending.

accepted means the provider accepted an attempt, not that the phone displayed it.
Only a proven pre-send failure or explicit HTTP 429/503 response is retryable.
An ambiguous upload, unexpected response or other 5xx result is terminal uncertain
to avoid duplicating a notification that may already have been accepted.

Focused verification from the repository root:

    php tests/phone-push-transport-v1.php
    PHP_BINARY=php node tests/phone-push-transport-crypto-v1.mjs

The PHP suite verifies all production-file SHA-256 hashes, the Composer lock and
the complete retained license copies without any network access. It also includes
the published RFC 8291 known-answer vector, SSRF/pinning, TLS/redirect/proxy
settings, bounded response readers and provider outcomes.
The Node suite independently decrypts actual PHP-generated records, rejects a
modified GCM record and verifies VAPID signatures/claims using Node/OpenSSL.
On PHP 8.1 the PHP suite verifies the guard without loading vendor code. Crypto
interoperability and real transport capability require the supported worker.
Neither suite contacts a push service or uses real device credentials.

To check an extracted deployment package with the same offline integrity tests,
point only the test suite at that package's bundle:

    VP3_PHONE_PUSH_VERIFY_BUNDLE=/path/to/extracted/vendor/web-push-v1 php tests/phone-push-transport-v1.php

The runtime manifest excludes the same Markdown and repository/tool/test
metadata directories omitted by the production package. All runtime code and
all original license files remain covered. This verification variable exists
only in the test; the production helper always loads its fixed local bundle.
